title: Regular sequence on the closed fibre of a flat local homomorphism
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ and $(S,\mathfrak n)$ be Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (commutative rings with exactly one maximal ideal, $\mathfrak m$ resp. $\mathfrak n$) and $\varphi:R\to S$ a ring homomorphism which is local ($\varphi(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$) and flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $\mathfrak mS$ be the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak m)$, let $c\ge0$ and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in S$, and suppose that the images $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c$ of the $f_j$ in $S/\mathfrak mS$ form a regular sequence in the ring $S/\mathfrak mS$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Then $f_1,\dots,f_c$ is a regular sequence in $S$, and for every $0\le i\le c$ the quotient $S/(f_1,\dots,f_i)S$, an $R$-module via $\varphi$, is a flat $R$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MG (lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence, algebra.tex line 23492; proof: induction and Lemma Tag 00MF lemma-grothendieck, line 23480). Tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00MG,algebra-lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence; 00MF,algebra-lemma-grothendieck)

proof.text: For $0\le i\le c$ put $S_i=S/(f_1,\dots,f_i)S$, with $S_0=S$, and write $\bar S=S/\mathfrak mS$. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], multiplication by the image of $f_{i+1}$ is injective on $\bar S/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_i)\bar S$ for every $i<c$, and the final quotient $\bar S/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)\bar S$ is nonzero. This quotient is the closed fibre $S_i/\mathfrak mS_i$ when $i=c$; the same identification holds for each prefix by the third isomorphism theorem. As every prefix quotient surjects onto the nonzero final quotient, each $S_i/\mathfrak mS_i$ is nonzero. In particular the ideal $(f_1,\dots,f_i)S$ is proper; since $S$ is local, it lies in $\mathfrak n$, and each $S_i$ is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n/(f_1,\dots,f_i)S$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00MG (lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence), lines 23492-23504: preparation for the stated induction; quotient and local-ring details written out from Definition Tag 00LF

proof.text: We prove by induction on $i$ that $S_i$ is flat as an $R$-module and $f_1,\dots,f_i$ is a weakly regular sequence in $S$ (each $f_j$ acts injectively on $S_{j-1}$). For $i=0$ the sequence is empty and $S_0=S$ is $R$-flat by the hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The map $R\to S_0$ is the given local homomorphism; the ring and closed-fibre conditions required for the induction are established in step 1.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00MG (lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence), line 23503: induction, base case expanded

proof.text: Suppose $i<c$ and $S_i$ is $R$-flat. The map $R\to S_i$ is local: its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak n/(f_1,\dots,f_i)S$ by step 1 and the image of $\mathfrak m$ lies in it. Its closed fibre is $S_i/\mathfrak mS_i\cong\bar S/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_i)\bar S$, on which multiplication by the class of $f_{i+1}$ is injective by step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-mod-injective] to this local map with $M=N=S_i$ (the target is $R$-flat by induction, and $N$ is finite over the Noetherian ring $S_i$, generated by $1$) and $u:S_i\to S_i$, $a\mapsto f_{i+1}a$. The reduction of $u$ modulo $\mathfrak m$ is that injective multiplication map. Hence $u$ is injective and its cokernel $S_i/f_{i+1}S_i\cong S_{i+1}$ is $R$-flat. Thus the next element is a nonzerodivisor on $S_i$, and the induction advances.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MF (lemma-grothendieck), lines 23480-23490, applied inductively as in Lemma Tag 00MG (lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence), lines 23492-23504; 00MF itself follows directly from Lemma Tag 00ME (lemma-mod-injective), lines 23424-23477

proof.text: At $i=c$, the induction gives $R$-flatness of every $S_i$ and injective multiplication by each $f_i$ on $S_{i-1}$. Step 1 gives $S_c\ne0$ because its quotient by $\mathfrak mS_c$ is nonzero. These are exactly the two conditions of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $f_1,\dots,f_c$ in $S$, including the empty-sequence case $c=0$ (then $S/\mathfrak mS\ne0$). The displayed $S_i$ are the quotients in the conclusion, so all are flat over $R$.
